scope: Repair shared scheduling and handoffs; preserve running workers. No coordinator-authored translation.
contract:
The owner clarified that the coordinator must repair the process, not personally translate. Preserve the six linguistic streams and sole shared technical stream. The coordinator does not create target wording or ad hoc per-language patches. Preserve all current assignments, frozen versions and accepted receipts. Every model remains fresh explicit Sol/high/OpenAI; no Astra, inherited history or extra workers.

The observer now quietly waits for a version-matching independently reviewed resource dependency. A blocked language result may retain its own exact nextTask with kind work, title, owning brief and briefSha256, together with its current technicalHandoffs. No prepared finite task means no automatic model launch. Unchanged source flags, draft files and bookkeeping do not wake a model. Source/glossary/haiku/native holds remain explicit; no gate is waived.

Use the SAME protocol for all six locales. For each fulfilled EXISTING request, the technical producer writes a JSON delivery with schemaVersion:1, kind:locale-resource-dependency, locale, requestId, request:{path,sha256} pointing to the EXACT latest original language handoff, consumptionReady:true, releaseAccepted:false, producerRuntime:{path,sha256}, inputs:[{path,sha256}], outputs:[{path,sha256}]. Inputs include EVERY recursively declared path/sha256 binding in that request. Outputs identify the actual nonempty saved game resources, not only a report, inside the technical lane write scope. Bind the complete finite requiredResult of that request, including full corpus/role requirements where specified; a partial family candidate does not fulfill a full-stage request. Static consumption does not grant native/application/release authority.

Add a row to the ALREADY REQUIRED independent review of that actual resource delivery. The row's source is the exact UTF-8 TEXT of the original language handoff file, target is the exact UTF-8 TEXT of the new delivery JSON, and sourceSha256/targetSha256 are their exact file hashes. Use a stable distinct id such as dependency-delivery:<locale>:<requestId>. Read and verify the actual delivered resources and every prerequisite; do not pass a schema alone. Keep the original author and independent reviewer different fresh verified processes. Do not create a paid phase solely to acknowledge or publish a completed receipt.

Only a clean COMPLETE technical REVIEW result may publish dependencyDeliveries:[{request:{path,sha256},delivery:{path,sha256},reviewId:<assigned row id>}]. Here request points to the corresponding technical INBOX ENVELOPE, while delivery.request points to its original language handoff. Include the delivery and reviews among normal evidence pins. The observer checks the assigned exact versions, clean judgments, independence, runtime model/provider, input and actual output hashes, then atomically publishes an immutable inbox/ready/<original-request-sha256>.json. Existing resolvedTechnicalHandoffs accounting remains separate. Ready receipts are independent per request, not a multi-request transaction; never claim all requests committed after a partial publication.

The waiting language lane revalidates that exact receipt and all bytes, consumes it once, and continues its own previously prepared finite consumption task. It does not retranslate unchanged wording or restart common engineering. In the phase task, dependencyReceipt names the exact pin to consume FIRST. Preserve receipt and output versions. If a real unrelated blocker remains, record it and stop unchanged model continuation. No game, GUI, screenshot, installer, owner-game write, publication, deployment, server lifecycle or Git authority is added.

A pending nextTask waits for ALL its current technicalHandoffs by default. It may declare dependencyRequests as an exact nonempty subset of those pins when its finite task needs only that subset. The observer rechecks every required receipt and wakes only if a newly unconsumed version is present. dependencyReceipts contains all checked receipt pins; dependencyReceipt is the first pin for compatibility. Consumers verify these receipts but never publish missing producer receipts.
